turn.context: Tojo · new rule: learning from your replies
turn.subject: reply-check-rule
turn.user_message: Flag each miss as high, medium or low. Send the history and the recommended change, once at the end of the day. A back-end agent reads Tojo's report, adds its own view, works with my team, and updates the files for the next day.

text: That changes two things from my last answer. Tojo now writes his own suggested changes, not just records. And a back-end agent replaces the nightly review, adding its own view before your team sees anything.
Every miss gets a priority, and nothing leaves the chat during the day. One report goes out at the end of the day, with the full history behind each miss.
bullets: I'd set end of day at midnight, India time, the same moment the summary pages refresh. Changes your team approves are then in the files Tojo reads the next morning.
This needs three pieces: Tojo's rule, the format of his daily report, and the back-end agent's own skill for reading it. The report format is what joins the two agents, so it should be settled first.
chat.pointer: Tap each step to see who acts, and each priority to see what puts a miss there.

items.title: High
items.text: Tojo got something wrong, or the user said plainly he missed the point.
more_points: The user says Tojo has not understood.
The rephrase after a reset also missed.
A wrong fact or figure from a reference file.
A figure Tojo made up, or one from another hospital.

items.title: Medium
items.text: The user did not go along with Tojo, without saying why.
more_points: Two misses in a row that set off a reset, where the rephrase then worked.
Tojo's question or figure request ignored.

items.title: Low
items.text: A small slip the user recovered from on their own.
more_points: A single ignored question the user answered a turn later.
Too long, or the drawing repeats the chat, with no complaint.
An unclear word the user asked about once.
